=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12651-12669 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The poller trusts retry-state JSON (`non_retryable`, failure count) from the editable final-PR body without verifying its author, and uses it to park the project (`integration_sync_status=escalated`). The reviewers cite these places: `_integration_conflict_park_if_stuck`, the retry-state read at ~12790 (`extract_autofix_resolver_retry_state_from_pr_body`), lines 9415-9424, 12786-12793 and 12659-12666.
  WHY: Anyone who can edit the PR body can force a park. The reviewers disagree on severity: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 rated it NIT with confidence 2 and said the trust pattern already exists; openai_gpt-6-luna rated it MAJOR; google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite gave no severity. The highest is used. minimax_minimax-m3 and qwen_qwen3_7-plus dismissed it as pre-existing.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12808, 12821-12822 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: `INTEGRATION_PARK_REBUILD_NOTE` is passed as a prefix assignment on a function call and may leak into the second call site at 12821-12822, contaminating `park_err`.
  WHY: google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite says non-POSIX bash persists the variable, which would cause repeated notifications. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3 and qwen_qwen3_7-plus rejected the claim, saying default bash scopes the assignment to the call. Gemini gave no severity, so medium is a placeholder.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12688-12699 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The park function does not check whether writing the parked state (`jq`/`mv`) succeeded before it posts the tracking comment, sends the Telegram warning and returns success.
  WHY: If the write fails, the persisted state is unchanged, so the next poll tick parks again and notifications repeat.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:_integration_conflict_park_if_stuck (read of INTEGRATION_PARK_REBUILD_NOTE) | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: `INTEGRATION_PARK_REBUILD_NOTE` comes from `BRANCH_REBUILD_ESCALATED_ERROR` and is appended unfiltered to `integration_sync_last_error`, the tracking comment and the Telegram message.
  WHY: The text is internal, so the risk is low. The reviewer suggests truncating it, for example `${INTEGRATION_PARK_REBUILD_NOTE:0:300}`. This was a hardening suggestion with risk score 1; the severity is inferred.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
(No task gaps reported.)
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:`_integration_conflict_park_if_stuck` and the retry-state read at ~12790 (`extract_autofix_resolver_retry_state_from_pr_body`) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The retry state comes from the editable final-PR body and its author is not verified, so anyone with PR-edit rights can set `non_retryable=true` or a count at the cap and park the project.
  WHY: This is not new trust, because the existing `resolver_retry_escalated` and `head_sha` checks already read the same block. A park is cleared by any push to the head.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:`_integration_conflict_park_if_stuck`, where `INTEGRATION_PARK_REBUILD_NOTE` is read (hardening suggestion, risk score 1)
  PROBLEM: The note comes from `BRANCH_REBUILD_ESCALATED_ERROR` and is appended unfiltered to `integration_sync_last_error`, the tracking comment and the Telegram message.
  WHY: It is internal text, so the risk is low. Suggested fix: truncate it to a fixed length (about 1 line changed).
- The reviewer dropped the "INTEGRATION_PARK_REBUILD_NOTE leaks between calls" finding, because the script never enables POSIX mode.
- All other categories: NONE. No task gaps.
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12651-12669 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The poller accepts `AUTOFIX_RESOLVER_RETRY_STATE_V1` JSON from the mutable final-PR body and uses it to set `integration_sync_status=escalated`.
  WHY: Anyone who can edit the PR body can inject `non_retryable=true` or change the failure counts to force a park.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12808, 12821-12822 | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `INTEGRATION_PARK_REBUILD_NOTE` is passed as a prefix assignment on a function call and is never cleared.
  WHY: The reviewer says non-POSIX bash persists the variable, so the second call inherits the stale note. That would contaminate `park_err` and cause repeated Telegram and tracking comments.
- Hardening suggestion (risk score 1, about 5 lines): inside `_integration_conflict_park_if_stuck`, read the note into a local variable with `local park_rebuild_note="${INTEGRATION_PARK_REBUILD_NOTE:-}"`.
- All other categories: NONE.
=== END FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===

=== FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:9415-9424, 12786-12793, 12659-12666 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The poller accepts the last valid retry-state JSON block in the final PR body without verifying who wrote it, then trusts `non_retryable` and `consecutive_failure_count` to park the project.
  WHY: A user who can edit the PR description can add a block with the current `head_sha` and `non_retryable: true`. The next poll tick then sets `integration_sync_status=escalated` and skips resolver and judge dispatches until the head changes.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:12688-12699 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The park function does not check whether writing the parked state succeeded before posting the tracking comment, sending the Telegram warning and returning success.
  WHY: If `jq` or `mv` fails, the persisted state is unchanged. The same retry state then triggers parking again on the next tick, so notifications repeat and the park is not durable.
=== END FINDINGS FROM openai_gpt-6-luna ===
